Subject: Kernel squad hiring prioritization matrix

Team —

Attached is v3 of the hiring prioritization matrix for the kernel squad (attached + sheet link below). This tries to make the trade-offs explicit across three axes: near-term latency wins, medium-term throughput gains, and long-term maintenance risk. Key context: Q1 budget assumes 6 new slots for runtime/kernel roles; we need to decide which roles to commit now and which to defer to Q2.

High level recommendations (see matrix for per-role scoring):
- 2x Kernel SRE (production reliability) — high latency/availability impact, medium cost
- 2x Compiler Engineer (quantization/kernels) — high throughput and cost impact, higher ramp time
- 2x Runtime SWE (integration + batching) — fast ramp, moderate perf impact

Asks:
1) Confirm which 6 slots we greenlight for Q1 by EOD next Tuesday (11/10).
2) If approving Compiler hires, confirm willingness to commit 9-month ramp before steady-state throughput benefits.
3) Any objections to reallocating 1 of the Runtime SWE slots to a Kernel SRE if SRE risk looks higher after hiring interviews.

Attachments: <attachment: kernel_prioritization_matrix_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)>
Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1KERNELMATRIX/edit#gid=0

Thanks —
Rishi

Rishi — thanks for pulling this together, helpful framing. A couple of quick questions before I can sign off: 

- Can you add expected monthly run-rate delta (post-onboard) for each role? That will make budget review with finance much easier.
- For the Compiler hires, do we have candidate pipelines already? I see a note about longer ramp but curious if we have 2-3 screened candidates in process.

Also: I think we should hold one slot flexible for urgent SRE coverage (on-call risk) vs. compiler. If the SRE interview loop finds an immediate senior candidate, we should be able to convert.

Quick note: Marissa, can you add the run-rate numbers into the sheet (column H) and share latest compensation bands?

Kimberly Park

Kimberly / Rishi — I reviewed the matrix and did a quick back-of-envelope for run-rate. Two thoughts: 

1) If we go 2 Compiler + 2 Runtime + 2 Kernel SRE as proposed, estimated incremental monthly run-rate ~ $162k (headcount + recruitment + ramp allowances). I put the detailed numbers in the sheet (row 23).
2) Given SUP-1428 (kernel CI flakiness) and the on-call load over the last month, I strongly prefer prioritizing 1 extra Kernel SRE over a Runtime SWE. Suggested Q1 slots: 3x Kernel SRE, 1x Compiler, 2x Runtime SWE.

If we can only get two senior SREs in Q1, we should push the second Compiler hire to Q2 rather than the Runtime role — the system availability risk is higher.

Attaching the headcount impact chart I referenced: <attachment: headcount_impact_chart.pdf (application/pdf)>

Marcus

All — after reading the updated sheet and Marcus's notes, I'm prepared to approve the Q1 slate with the following firming: 

Approved Q1 hires (6 slots):
- 3x Kernel SRE (two senior, one mid) — priority A
- 1x Compiler Engineer — priority B (start search immediately, flexible on seniority)
- 2x Runtime SWE — priority B (one can be contractor-to-FTE if pipeline shows faster ramp)

Conditions and next steps:
- Kimberly/Marissa: please confirm monthly run-rate numbers and compensation bands in the sheet by EOD 11/18 so Finance can finalize the budget allocation.
- Marcus: when you post the Kernel SRE job, include explicit on-call expectations and the CI improvement KR so candidates see the priority.
- Rishi: if strong senior Compiler candidates appear, you may convert 1 Runtime slot to Compiler but please notify leadership first.
